The failing test `testEventsScheduling` creates a DormandPrince853Integrator ODE solver, adds two different event handlers and their associated step handlers, and integrates a simple harmonic oscillator system from time 0.5 to 10. The bug report indicates a problem in the ODE solver event management related to multiple concurrent event types: when one event handler requests a RESET_STATE during an event, other event handlers that did not trigger an event in the same step are not updated correctly due to an early return.

The test involves two event handlers triggering events at different phases (sine and cosine zeros) and so stresses this multi-event coordination.

The DormandPrince853Integrator constructor snippet shows it calls a superclass constructor with step interpolators and tolerances, but the actual integration logic with event handling is not shown.

Multiple attempts to fetch the integrate method of DormandPrince853Integrator failed due to ambiguity or multiple overloads; many match similar signature methods exist but with different arg types or class variants, possibly due to overloads or internal class variants using ExpandableStatefulODE rather than FirstOrderDifferentialEquations.

Given the bug report and test, the most relevant code will be the integrate method(s) handling multiple events, specifically the portions invoking eventOccurred on event handlers and handling their event types (e.g. RESET_STATE). The issue is caused likely by an early return preventing the update of event states for handlers not triggering an event in that step.

Next, I will locate the integrate(org.apache.commons.math3.ode.FirstOrderDifferentialEquations,double,double[],double,double[]) method specifically for DormandPrince853Integrator or its superclasses. If not found, I will check the superclasses (likely AdaptiveStepsizeIntegrator or the base ODE integrator classes) for event handling during integration, especially looking for where event handlers are called in eventOccurred and how their results influence the loop and update of other event handlers states.

I will now try to retrieve the integrate method for the superclass AdaptiveStepsizeIntegrator, which is a known superclass of DormandPrince853Integrator and where the core integration with event management is implemented.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
